I need an EXHAUSTIVE field-by-field enumeration. Read these BASE SFCC component sources (read them fully, don't skim):
- node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/item-variant/index.jsx
- node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/item-variant/item-image.jsx
- node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/item-variant/item-name.jsx
- node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/item-variant/item-attributes.jsx
- Also follow into any helper they call, e.g. node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/image-groups-utils.js (or similarly named — find it), and getDisplayVariationValues / filterImageGroups in node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils.js
- node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/display-price/index.jsx (and any sub-files in that folder)

TASK: produce a complete list of every property that is read off the *variant object* (which is `{...basketProductItem, ...productFromUseProducts, price: basketItem.price}`) by each of those components — including nested paths (e.g. `imageGroups[].images[].link`, `variationAttributes[].values[].name`, `type.master`, `master.masterId`, etc.). For each field, note whether it comes from the BASKET product item or from the PRODUCT (useProducts) response — some fields exist on both.

Pay special attention to:
1. `item-image.jsx` — exactly which imageGroup viewType(s) it requests, and exactly which image properties it reads (link? disBaseLink? alt? title?). Does it read `variationValues` off the basket item to filter image groups? Which variation attribute id does it filter on?
2. `item-attributes.jsx` — which fields, including `variationValues`, `variationAttributes`, `quantity`, `inventory`, `c_*` customs, `itemText`, `priceAdjustments`, `bonusDiscountLineItemId`, `bundledProductItems`.
3. `item-name.jsx` — does it read `name`, `productName`, `id`, `productId`, `master.masterId`, `type.*`? Does it build a link, and from what field?
4. `display-price/index.jsx` — which properties of the `priceData` object it reads, and how it renders `listPrice` vs `currentPrice` vs `pricePerUnit`, and what `quantity` prop does when passed vs omitted.

Then compare against this exact SCAPI field-projection string a PR adds to the `useProducts` call, plus `expand: ['images','variations']` and `allImages: true`:

(data.(id,name,master.(masterId),type.(bundle,master,set),c_isSale,variationAttributes.(id,name,values.(value,name)),imageGroups[viewType=small].(viewType,images.(link,disBaseLink,alt),variationAttributes.(id,values.(value)))))

Report: (a) the full read-field list per component with file:line references, (b) any field that is READ but NOT covered by that projection string, (c) any field in the projection that nothing reads (dead selection). Be precise about nested selection semantics — e.g. does selecting `imageGroups[viewType=small]` cover what item-image needs, and does `variationAttributes.(id,name,values.(value,name))` cover what item-attributes needs.

Note: `expand` controls which top-level expansions SCAPI returns (images, variations, prices, availability, promotions, options, set_products, recommendations, shipping_methods, page_meta_tags). Consider whether removing `prices` from expand removes `product.price` / `tieredPrices` / `productPromotions` and whether anything downstream needs those. Be explicit and cite file:line for every claim.

- playwright-skill: Complete browser automation with Playwright. Auto-detects dev servers, writes clean test scripts to /tmp. Test pages, fill forms, take screenshots, check responsive design, validate UX, test login flows, check links, automate any browser task. Use when user wants to test websites, automate browser interactions, validate web functionality, or perform any browser-based testing.
- zimmerMANNBuild: The builder. Executes an approved zimmerMANNPreBuild plan through a closed-loop multi-agent workflow — implement, test, scope-check, score, rework until passed — committing each step and handing off to zimmerMANNPostBuild. Also handles rework from CodeRabbit or reviewer change requests after a PR is open.
- zimmerMANNDevImprover: Looks back over completed build work and improves the build chain. Reads the session transcripts and run artefacts for named stories, diagnoses where the loop failed and whose gap it was, checks whether the skills still cite things that are true, and proposes concrete edits to the build skills and loop agents — applied only on Marcel's explicit go.
- zimmerMANNDevOps: Runs deploys, promotions across environments, tags, release cuts and rollbacks on the Zimmermann PWA Kit. Verifies pipeline state live before every action, shows what each environment is running, and executes only on explicit approval. Reports broken gates and stops rather than working around them.
- zimmerMANNPostBuild: The senior dev pass after a build. Audits what zimmerMANNBuild produced against zimmerMANNPreBuild's plan and findings, runs a whole-feature sweep for uniform defects, writes the PR body, and owns the review conversation — pushing and replying only on Marcel's go.
- zimmerMANNPreBuild: The gate and planner before any Zimmermann PWA Kit build work. Gathers and cross-checks every source — Jira, Confluence, the FED handbook, the codebase and Figma — flags every gap and misalignment, then produces an executable closed-loop build plan and hands off to zimmerMANNBuild. Use at the start of any story, ticket or build task.
- zimmerMANNReview: Reviews someone else's PR as FED Lead. Establishes ground truth, fans out audit angles, verifies every finding before it is raised, then presents for adjudication — Marcel decides the verdict, and comments post only on his go. Loops until the PR is approved.
- zimmerMANNRevImprover: Looks back over completed PR reviews and improves how Marcel reviews. Reads the PR outcome and the review session transcript to judge whether each finding held up, whether anything was missed, and how the review was actually conducted — then proposes concrete edits to zimmerMANNReview, applied only on his explicit go.
- zimmerMANNSprinter: The skill for sprint and agile ceremonies as FED Lead — backlog refinement, sprint planning, standups, retros, and prep for any meeting. Reads Jira and Confluence, drafts what you need to take into the room, and writes to Jira only on your explicit go.
- audit-tier: Identify the protection tier, owner, and import blast radius of a file or directory under overrides/. Use before editing anything you're unsure about.
- code-quality: Audit recently changed or specified files for code quality issues — naming, circular imports, TypeScript coverage, test/story existence, and structural debt. Read-only. Use after implementing a feature or before opening a PR.
- code-review: AI-powered code review using CodeRabbit. Default code-review skill. Trigger for any explicit review request AND autonomously when the agent thinks a review is needed (code/PR/quality/security).
- contentful-register-component: Register a Zimmermann React component with Contentful Studio Experiences. Use when a developer asks to register, add, or expose a React component to Contentful, or when they need to create a Contentful component definition for an existing component.
- feature-spec: Turn a plain-English feature request into a scoped implementation plan before any code is written. Asks one clarifying question at a time, then produces a spec Claude Code can execute safely. Use this before starting any non-trivial implementation session.
- generate-changelog: Generate a release changelog from conventional commits and upstream baseline notes. Produces audience-specific outputs for the dev team, QA, product, and GitHub Release. Use before cutting a release branch or when preparing release notes.
- new-component: Scaffold a new Zimmermann component under overrides/app/components/ — TypeScript, Chakra-first, with a paired Storybook story. Use whenever a new custom component is needed.
- onboarding: Interactive onboarding for new developers and QA engineers joining the Zimmermann PWA Kit project. Asks role at the start, checks the mechanical setup items, then orients the person to the rules and tools relevant to their role and squad. Run this in the first Claude Code session on a new machine or a first day on the project.
- pr-checklist: Generate a PR description and merge checklist based on the files changed on the current branch. Pairs with /code-quality.
- project-init: One-time project setup walkthrough. Runs the state detection script, fixes automatable items, asks one question at a time for human-input items, and updates the 7.1c CI/CD & Environment Setup Checklist Confluence page as each item is confirmed. Run this once when setting up the project for the first time, or when returning to check setup status.
- qa-generate: Generate a Gherkin .feature file and Playwright test spec from a Jira story. Human-in-the-lead — Lead QA validates the .feature before Playwright is generated. Use for any new storefront user journey that needs E2E test coverage.

Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'inspect' returns the accessibility tree of the front app (what a screen reader reads, which can differ from what is drawn) as JSON — per element: type, label, value, frame [x,y,width,height] in device points from the top-left, traits the type does not imply, enabled only when false, children. Call 'inspect' before a 'tap' on anything you have not located in this screen's tree, before answering what text a screen shows, and before reporting a control's state (a switch's value, whether a button is enabled, which tab is selected) or whether a sheet, alert or other modal is in front (the result says so) — never guess coordinates from memory of similar apps, and do not 'screenshot' for these. Go straight to 'screenshot' for color, images, and layout. Three reads: no marker and no x/y = the whole visible tree (the safe default when you do not know the exact label); marker = the first element, in tree order, whose label contains that CASE-SENSITIVE substring — a title can match before the button with the same text, so check the matched element's type; x/y = the element drawn on top at that point, as a tap would find it, with its descendants (a point between controls hits their container). If a marker misses or returns the wrong element, read the whole tree instead of guessing or screenshotting. Then tap the center of the target's frame. Hidden, off-screen, and illegibly small elements are omitted and counted; text longer than its area shows is cut (it ends with ...). Only the x/y read resolves occlusion, and only by bars and containers it can recognize: a frame from the whole-tree or marker read that overlaps a later sibling (a tab bar, a sheet) may be covered, so before tapping it read x/y at its center; a point on a sheet's blank area can still read the content behind it, so when the result reports a modal, stay inside it. A tree over the size cap loses its deepest levels first and says so — narrow with marker, or with x/y on the target itself: a point in a gap answers the container around it, which is no smaller; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the currently attached simulator, or the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

marker.description: For 'inspect': return only the first element (tree order, with its descendants) whose match_key attribute contains this case-sensitive substring — pass the label text exactly as the tree or the user wrote it, and prefer a distinctive fragment over a guess at capitalization. Omit for the whole tree (the safe default), or pass x/y instead for the element under a point.

match_key.description: For 'inspect' with 'marker': the attribute to match — label (default), value, or role (the element type, e.g. Button, Switch, TabBar — pass the exact name).

8	/**
9	 * Find the ImageGroup that matches the criteria supplied
10	 *
11	 * @param {Object} imageGroups - The product/variations image groups you want to search.
12	 * @param {Object} options - Search criteria to match on the ImageGroup object.
13	 * @param {string} options.viewType - Typically this refers to image sizes like small, medium, large. But can vary based on your back-end configuration.
14	 * @param {Object} options.selectedVariationAttributes - A key/value object consisting of attibute id's and their values.
15	 * @returns {Object} - The ImageGroup matching the search criteria
16	 */
17	export const findImageGroupBy = (imageGroups = [], options) => {
18	    let {viewType, selectedVariationAttributes = {}} = options
19	
20	    // Start by filtering out any imageGroup that isn't the correct viewType.
21	    imageGroups = imageGroups.filter(
22	        ({viewType: imageGroupViewType}) => imageGroupViewType === viewType
23	    )
24	
25	    // Not all variation attributes are reflected in images. For example, you probably
26	    // won't have a separate image group for various sizes, but you might for colors. For that
27	    // reason we need to know what are valid attribute values to filter on.
28	    const refinableAttributeIds = [
29	        ...new Set(
30	            imageGroups
31	                .reduce((acc, {variationAttributes = []}) => [...acc, ...variationAttributes], [])
32	                .map(({id}) => id)
33	        )
34	    ]
35	
36	    // Update the `selectedVariationAttributes` by filtering out the attributes that have no
37	    // representation in this imageGroup.
38	    selectedVariationAttributes = Object.keys(selectedVariationAttributes).reduce((acc, curr) => {
39	        return refinableAttributeIds.includes(curr)
40	            ? {
41	                  ...acc,
42	                  [`${curr}`]: selectedVariationAttributes[curr]
43	              }
44	            : acc
45	    }, {})
46	
47	    // Find the image group that has all the all the selected variation value attributes.
48	    imageGroups = imageGroups.find(({variationAttributes = []}) => {
49	        const selectedIds = Object.keys(selectedVariationAttributes)
50	
51	        return selectedIds.every((selectedId) => {
52	            const selectedValue = selectedVariationAttributes[selectedId]
53	
54	            return variationAttributes.find(
55	                ({id, values}) =>
56	                    id === selectedId && values.every(({value}) => value === selectedValue)
57	            )
58	        })
59	    })
60	
61	    return imageGroups
62	}

10	/**
11	 * Get the human-friendly version of the variation values that users have selected.
12	 * Useful for displaying these values in the UI.
13	 *
14	 * @param {Object} variationAttributes - The products variation attributes.
15	 * @param {Object} values - The variations selected attribute values.
16	 * @returns {Object} - A key value map of the display name and display value.
17	 *

23	 * // returns { "Colour": "royal" }
24	 */
25	export const getDisplayVariationValues = (variationAttributes, values = {}) => {
26	    if (!variationAttributes || !Array.isArray(variationAttributes)) {
27	        return {}
28	    }
29	
30	    const returnVal = Object.entries(values).reduce((acc, [id, value]) => {
31	        const attribute = variationAttributes.find(({id: attributeId}) => attributeId === id)
32	        if (!attribute || !attribute.values) {
33	            return acc
34	        }
35	
36	        const attributeValue = attribute.values.find(
37	            ({value: attributeValue}) => attributeValue === value
38	        )
39	
40	        if (attributeValue) {
41	            return {
42	                ...acc,
43	                [attribute.name]: attributeValue.name
44	            }
45	        }
46	        return acc

51	/**
52	 * Normalizes data for product sets and product bundles into the same format
53	 * Useful for operations that apply to both product sets and product bundles
54	 * Creates deep clones of child products to avoid mutation issues
55	 *
56	 * @param {Object} product - A product set or product bundle
57	 * @returns {Object} - returns normalized product if product is a set/bundle, otherwise returns original product
58	 */
59	export const normalizeSetBundleProduct = (product) => {
60	    if (!product?.type.set && !product?.type.bundle) return product
61	
62	    const childProducts = product?.type.set
63	        ? product.setProducts.map((child) => {
64	              return {
65	                  product: {...child},
66	                  quantity: null
67	              }
68	          })
69	        : product.bundledProducts.map((child) => {
70	              return {
71	                  ...child,
72	                  product: {...child.product}
73	              }
74	          })

76	    return {
77	        ...product,
78	        childProducts
79	    }

82	/**
83	 * Creates an array of product items used to update the child variant selections for a product bundle,
84	 * usually in an updateItemToBasket/updateItemsToBasket shopper baskets API call
85	 *
86	 * @param {Object} bundle - A product that is a bundle.
87	 * @param {Array} childProductSelections - An array of the bundle child products with a selected variant.
88	 *      Each item in the array should have the product, variant, and quantity.
89	 * @returns {Array} - an array of bundle child product items that have the updated variant
90	 */
91	export const getUpdateBundleChildArray = (bundle, childProductSelections) => {
92	    const itemsToBeUpdated = []
93	    bundle?.bundledProductItems?.forEach((bundleChild) => {
94	        const childSelection = childProductSelections?.find(
95	            (childProduct) =>
96	                childProduct.product?.id === bundleChild.productId ||
97	                childProduct.product?.itemId === bundleChild.itemId
98	        )
99	
100	        const selectedProductId = childSelection?.variant?.productId || childSelection?.product?.id
101	
102	        // only update the item if the selected product is different from what's in the current bundle
103	        if (childSelection && selectedProductId !== bundleChild.productId) {
104	            itemsToBeUpdated.push({
105	                itemId: bundleChild.itemId,
106	                productId: selectedProductId,
107	                quantity: childSelection.quantity ?? bundleChild.quantity
108	            })
109	        }
110	    })
111	    return itemsToBeUpdated
112	}

114	/**
115	 * This function extract the price information of a given product
116	 * If a product is a master,
117	 *  currentPrice: get the lowest price (including promotional prices) among variants
118	 *  listPrice: get the list price of the variant that has lowest price (including promotional price)
119	 *  maxPrice: the max price in tieredPrices of variant that has lowest price
120	 * @param {object} product - product detail object
121	 * @param {object} opts - options to pass into the function like intl, quantity, and currency
122	 */
123	export const getPriceData = (product, opts = {}) => {
124	    const {quantity = 1} = opts
125	    const isASet = product?.hitType === 'set' || !!product?.type?.set
126	    const isMaster = product?.hitType === 'master' || !!product?.type?.master
127	    let currentPrice
128	    let variantWithLowestPrice
129	    // grab the variant that has the lowest price (including promotional price)
130	    if (isMaster) {
131	        variantWithLowestPrice = findLowestPrice(product)
132	        currentPrice = variantWithLowestPrice?.minPrice
133	    } else {
134	        currentPrice = findLowestPrice(product)?.minPrice
135	    }
136	
137	    // since the price is the lowest value among price books, each product will have at lease a single item tiered price at quantity 1
138	    // the highest value of tieredPrices is presumptively the list price
139	    const tieredPrices = variantWithLowestPrice?.data?.tieredPrices || product?.tieredPrices || []
140	    const maxTieredPrice = tieredPrices?.length
141	        ? Math.max(...tieredPrices.map((item) => item.price))
142	        : undefined
143	    const highestTieredPrice = tieredPrices.find((tier) => tier.price === maxTieredPrice)
144	    const listPrice = highestTieredPrice?.price
145	
146	    // if a product has tieredPrices, get the tiered that has the higher closest quantity to current quantity
147	    const filteredTiered = tieredPrices.filter((tiered) => tiered.quantity <= quantity)
148	    const closestTieredPrice =
149	        filteredTiered.length &&
150	        filteredTiered.reduce((prev, curr) => {
151	            return Math.abs(curr.quantity - quantity) < Math.abs(prev.quantity - quantity)
152	                ? curr
153	                : prev
154	        })
155	    return {
156	        currentPrice,
157	        listPrice,
158	        pricePerUnit: product?.pricePerUnit,
159	        isOnSale: currentPrice < listPrice,
160	        isASet,
161	        isMaster,
162	        // For a product, set price is the lowest price of its children, so the price should be considered a range
163	        // For a master product, when it has more than 2 variants, we use the lowest priced variant, so it is  considered a range price
164	        //      but for master that has one variant, it is not considered range
165	        isRange: (isMaster && product?.variants?.length > 1) || isASet || false,
166	        // priceMax is for product set
167	        tieredPrice: closestTieredPrice?.price,
168	        maxPrice: product?.priceMax || maxTieredPrice
169	    }
170	}

172	/**
173	 * Filters the provided product `ImageGroups` array with the optional filters.
174	 *
175	 * @param {ImageGroup[]} imageGroups
176	 * @param {object} filters
177	 * @param {string} filters.viewType
178	 * @param {object} filters.variationValues
179	 *
180	 * @returns {ImageGroup[]} filteredImageGroups
181	 */
182	export const filterImageGroups = (imageGroups = [], filters) => {
183	    if (!filters) {
184	        throw new Error(`Missing required "filters" argument`)
185	    }
186	
187	    const {viewType, variationValues = {}} = filters
188	    // NOTE: For future feature enhancement compatibility we use an object for the `variationValues` as
189	    // we might want to filter on more than the one attribute id/value pair.
190	    const [selectedAttributeId, selectedAttributeValue] = Object.entries(variationValues)[0] || []
191	
192	    // Filters
193	    const typeFilter = viewType ? (group) => group.viewType === viewType : () => true
194	    const attributeFilter =
195	        !!selectedAttributeId && !!selectedAttributeValue
196	            ? ({variationAttributes = []}) =>
197	                  variationAttributes.some(
198	                      ({id, values}) =>
199	                          id === selectedAttributeId &&
200	                          !!values.find(({value}) => value === selectedAttributeValue)
201	                  )
202	            : () => true
203	
204	    return imageGroups?.filter(typeFilter)?.filter(attributeFilter)
205	}

207	/**
208	 * Provided a product this function will return the variation attibutes decorated with
209	 * `href` and `swatch` image for the given attribute values. This allows easier access
210	 * when creating components that commonly use this information.
211	 *
212	 * @param {Product} product
213	 * @param {object} opts
214	 * @param {string} opts.swatchViewType - The `viewTypeId` for the swatch image. Defaults to `swatch`.
215	 *
216	 * @returns {VariationAttributes[]} decoratedVariationAttributes
217	 */
218	export const getDecoratedVariationAttributes = (product, opts = {}) => {
219	    const swatchViewType = opts.swatchViewType || 'swatch'
220	
221	    return product?.variationAttributes?.map((variationAttribute) => ({
222	        ...variationAttribute,
223	        values: variationAttribute.values.map((value) => {
224	            const variationValues = {[variationAttribute.id]: value.value}
225	
226	            return {
227	                ...value,
228	                swatch: filterImageGroups(product.imageGroups, {
229	                    viewType: swatchViewType,
230	                    variationValues
231	                })?.[0]?.images[0],
232	                href: rebuildPathWithParams(
233	                    productUrlBuilder({id: product.productId}),

241	/**
242	 * Find the lowest price of a product, across all of its price books and promotions
243	 * @param {Object} product - product data from the API
244	 * @returns {Object|undefined} the lowest price for the given product. If it's a promotional price, the promotion will also be returned.
245	 */
246	export const findLowestPrice = (product) => {
247	    if (!product) return
248	
249	    // Look at all of the variants, only if it's a master product.
250	    // i.e. when a shopper has narrowed down to a variant, do not look into other variants
251	    const isMaster = product.hitType === 'master' || !!product.type?.master
252	    if (isMaster && !product.variants) {
253	        console.warn(
254	            'Expecting `product.variants` to exist. For more accuracy, please tweak your API request to ask for the variants details.'
255	        )
256	    }
257	    const array = isMaster && product.variants ? product.variants : [product]
258	
259	    const res = array.reduce(
260	        (prev, data) => {
261	            const promotions = data.productPromotions || []
262	            const [smallestPromotionalPrice, promo] = getSmallestValByProperty(
263	                promotions,
264	                'promotionalPrice'
265	            )
266	
267	            let salePrice = data.price
268	            let promotion = null
269	            if (smallestPromotionalPrice && smallestPromotionalPrice < data.price) {
270	                salePrice = smallestPromotionalPrice
271	                promotion = promo
272	            }
273	
274	            return salePrice < prev.minPrice ? {minPrice: salePrice, promotion, data} : prev
275	        },
276	        {minPrice: Infinity, promotion: null, data: null}
277	    )
278	    return {
279	        ...res,
280	        // when minPrice is infinity, meaning there is no variant with lowest price found, we rest the value to 0 as minPrice to be able to use this value on UI
281	        minPrice: res.minPrice === Infinity ? 0 : res.minPrice
282	    }
283	}

286	 * @private
287	 * Find the smallest value by key from a given array
288	 * @returns {Array} an array of such smallest value and the item containing this value
289	 * @example
290	 * const [value, itemContainingValue] = getSmallestValByProperty(array, key)
291	 */
292	const getSmallestValByProperty = (arr, key) => {
293	    if (!arr || !arr.length) return []
294	    if (!key) {
295	        throw new Error('Please specify a key.')
296	    }
297	    const filtered = arr.filter((item) => {
298	        const value = item[key]
299	        return value === 0 || value === '0' ? true : Number(value)
300	    })
301	    if (filtered.length === 0) return []
302	
303	    return filtered.reduce(
304	        (prev, item) => {
305	            const value = item[key]
306	            const [prevValue] = prev
307	            return value < prevValue ? [value, item] : prev
308	        },
309	        [Infinity, null]
310	    )
311	}

150	          priceData={priceData}
151	          quantity={variant?.quantity}
152	          listPriceProps={{ fontSize: 'sm' }}
153	          currentPriceProps={{ fontWeight: 'var(--zimm-font-weight-medium)' }}
154	        />
155	      )}
156	    </Stack>

3	/**
4	 * `c_maxOrderQuantity` is a Zimmermann-custom SFCC attribute — a real BM site preference
5	 * (Integer, default 3, min 1, per-site) surfaced onto the SCAPI product response via a
6	 * `dw.ocapi.shop.product.afterGET` hook, per Confluence `TSD-SFCC-268` (406913046). It has no
7	 * typed field on the base SDK's `Product` type — it only reaches this shape via that type's own
8	 * `{[key: string]: any}` index signature, the same situation
9	 * `overrides/app/pages/product-list/productListCardMapper.ts` lines 16-23 document for a
10	 * different custom attribute (`c_productBadges`). Narrowed here to a local type rather than
11	 * trusting `any` at the call site, per AGENTS.md's Gotchas: "Commerce SDK types not importable
12	 * ... declare a narrow local type."
13	 *
14	 * Typed `unknown`, not `number | undefined`: this function's whole job is validating a value
15	 * that may legitimately arrive absent, as `0`, negative, or non-numeric (see the pass criteria
16	 * this file's own test covers) — typing it as `number | undefined` would assert a guarantee the
17	 * real BM data doesn't have.
18	 *
19	 * As of this commit `TSD-SFCC-268` is still `v0.1 Draft` (Technical Lead sign-off Pending) and a
20	 * live dev-sandbox probe found no `c_maxOrderQuantity` on any product — the `afterGET` hook is
21	 * not deployed yet. Reading the field with the fallback below degrades to today's hardcoded
22	 * behaviour while that remains true, and picks up the real per-site value the day the hook ships,
23	 * with no further frontend change needed.
24	 */
25	type ProductWithMaxOrderQuantity = ShopperProductsTypes.Product & {
26	  c_maxOrderQuantity?: unknown;
27	};
28	
29	/**
30	 * Frontend fallback when no valid `c_maxOrderQuantity` is present. Matches
31	 * `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx`'s own `MAX_PURCHASE_QUANTITY` value (3) exactly
32	 * (see that file's lines 124-125: "Frontend-enforced limit (SFCC-196). SFCC has no platform
33	 * max-order-quantity field."), but is deliberately its own, independent constant rather than a
34	 * shared/promoted one — the TSD's resolution order is product override (SFCC-703) -> site
35	 * preference -> this hardcoded value, so a constant shared between the PDP and this cart-facing
36	 * util would need reworking the day the real per-site preference ships anyway.
37	 */
38	const DEFAULT_MAX_ORDER_QUANTITY = 3;
39	
40	/**
41	 * Reads the real per-product order-quantity cap off a SCAPI product response
42	 * (`c_maxOrderQuantity`), falling back to `DEFAULT_MAX_ORDER_QUANTITY` when the attribute is
43	 * absent or not a valid, usable cap (zero, negative, or non-numeric) — see this file's own
44	 * module docblock for why a shared constant is deliberately not used here.
45	 *
46	 * @param product A SCAPI product response (or product-shaped object) that may carry
47	 * `c_maxOrderQuantity`.
48	 * @returns The product's real max order quantity, or `DEFAULT_MAX_ORDER_QUANTITY` (3) when no
49	 * valid value is present.
50	 */
51	export const getMaxOrderQuantity = (product: ProductWithMaxOrderQuantity): number => {
52	  const value = product?.c_maxOrderQuantity;
53	  return typeof value === 'number' && Number.isFinite(value) && value > 0 ? value : DEFAULT_MAX_ORDER_QUANTITY;
54	};

15	const OUT_OF_STOCK = 'OUT_OF_STOCK'

18	const getInventoryById = (product, inventoryId) => {
19	    if (!inventoryId || !product?.inventories) {

25	// TODO: This needs to be refactored.

27	export const useDerivedProduct = (

29	    isProductPartOfSet = false,
30	    isProductPartOfBundle = false,
31	    pickupInStore = false,
32	    controlledVariationValues = null,
33	    onVariationChange = null

35	    const showLoading = !product
36	    const isProductABundle = product?.type?.bundle
37	    const stockLevel = product?.inventory?.stockLevel || 0
38	    const stepQuantity = product?.stepQuantity || 1
39	    const minOrderQuantity = stockLevel > 0 ? product?.minOrderQuantity || 1 : 0
40	    const initialQuantity = product?.quantity || product?.minOrderQuantity || 1
41	
42	    // used for product bundles when there are multiple products
43	    const lowestStockLevelProductName = product?.inventory?.lowestStockLevelProductName
44	    const intl = useIntl()
45	    const variant = useVariant(
46	        product,
47	        isProductPartOfSet,
48	        isProductPartOfBundle,
49	        controlledVariationValues
50	    )
51	    const isStandardProduct = product?.type?.item
52	    const variationParams = useVariationParams(
53	        product,
54	        isProductPartOfSet,
55	        isProductPartOfBundle,
56	        controlledVariationValues
57	    )
58	    const variationAttributes = useVariationAttributes(
59	        product,
60	        isProductPartOfSet,
61	        isProductPartOfBundle,
62	        controlledVariationValues,
63	        onVariationChange
64	    )
65	    const [quantity, setQuantity] = useState(initialQuantity)
66	    const {selectedStore} = useSelectedStore()
67	
68	    // A product is considered out of stock if the stock level is 0 or if we have all our
69	    // variation attributes selected, but don't have a variant. We do this because the API
70	    // will sometimes return all the variants even if they are out of stock, but for other
71	    // products it won't.
72	    const isOutOfStock =
73	        !stockLevel ||
74	        (!isProductABundle &&
75	            !variant &&
76	            !isStandardProduct &&
77	            Object.keys(variationParams).length === variationAttributes.length) ||
78	        (!isProductABundle && variant && !variant.orderable)
79	    const unfulfillable = stockLevel < quantity
80	
81	    // Product details for selected store
82	    const selectedStoreInventory = getInventoryById(product, selectedStore?.inventoryId)
83	    const selectedStoreStockLevel = selectedStoreInventory?.stockLevel || 0
84	    const selectedStoreLowestStockLevelProductName =
85	        selectedStoreInventory?.lowestStockLevelProductName
86	    // selectedStoreStockLevel and selectedStoreInventory are already variant specific,
87	    // so we don't need to check for variation attributes
88	    const isSelectedStoreOutOfStock = !selectedStoreStockLevel || !selectedStoreInventory?.orderable
89	    const selectedStoreUnfulfillable = selectedStoreStockLevel < quantity
90	
91	    // Use appropriate inventory based on pickup/delivery selection
92	    const currentStockLevel = pickupInStore ? selectedStoreStockLevel : stockLevel
93	    const currentLowestStockLevelProductName = pickupInStore
94	        ? selectedStoreLowestStockLevelProductName
95	        : lowestStockLevelProductName
96	    const currentIsOutOfStock = pickupInStore ? isSelectedStoreOutOfStock : isOutOfStock
97	    const currentUnfulfillable = pickupInStore ? selectedStoreUnfulfillable : unfulfillable
98	
99	    const inventoryMessages = {
100	        [OUT_OF_STOCK]: intl.formatMessage({
101	            defaultMessage: 'Out of stock',
102	            id: 'use_product.message.out_of_stock'
103	        }),
104	        [UNFULFILLABLE]: currentLowestStockLevelProductName
105	            ? intl.formatMessage(
106	                  {
107	                      defaultMessage: 'Only {stockLevel} left for {productName}!',
108	                      id: 'use_product.message.inventory_remaining_for_product'
109	                  },
110	                  {stockLevel: currentStockLevel, productName: currentLowestStockLevelProductName}
111	              )
112	            : intl.formatMessage(
113	                  {
114	                      defaultMessage: 'Only {stockLevel} left!',
115	                      id: 'use_product.message.inventory_remaining'
116	                  },
117	                  {stockLevel: currentStockLevel}
118	              )
119	    }
120	
121	    // showInventoryMessage controls if add to cart button is disabled
122	    const showInventoryMessage =
123	        (variant || isProductABundle || isStandardProduct) &&
124	        (currentIsOutOfStock || currentUnfulfillable)
125	    const inventoryMessage =
126	        (currentIsOutOfStock && inventoryMessages[OUT_OF_STOCK]) ||
127	        (currentUnfulfillable && inventoryMessages[UNFULFILLABLE])
128	
129	    // If the `initialQuantity` changes, update the state. This typically happens
130	    // when either the master product changes, or the inventory of the product changes
131	    // from out-of-stock to in-stock or vice versa.
132	    useEffect(() => {
133	        setQuantity(initialQuantity)
134	    }, [initialQuantity])
135	
136	    // Lump the out of stock/unfulfillable checks together for easier consumption
137	    return {
138	        showLoading,
139	        showInventoryMessage,
140	        inventoryMessage,
141	        variationAttributes,
142	        quantity,
143	        minOrderQuantity,
144	        stepQuantity,
145	        variationParams,
146	        setQuantity,
147	        variant,
148	        stockLevel,
149	        isOutOfStock,
150	        unfulfillable,
151	        isSelectedStoreOutOfStock: isSelectedStoreOutOfStock || selectedStoreUnfulfillable,
152	        selectedStore
153	    }

101	    isProductPartOfBundle = false,
102	    controlledVariationValues = null,
103	    onVariationChange = null

## One unverified syntax risk

`imageGroups[viewType=small]` is an attribute-predicate filter. There is **no precedent for it anywhere in base retail-react-app 10.0.0 or this repo** — every existing `select` is plain parenthesis projection (`'(data.(id,inventory,inventories,master))'`, `pages/cart/index.jsx:197` and `pages/product-detail/index.jsx:174`), and the repo has zero occurrences of `imageGroups[` in any `select` (grep-confirmed). I could not verify from the codebase that SCAPI's `select` grammar accepts a value predicate rather than an index. Worth an actual live probe against the sandbox before merge — if the predicate is rejected, the endpoint will either 400 or silently return no image groups at all.
